Record · Walter Hines Page · 1855–1918
A house directed
from London.
Garran Hill · Pinehurst, NC · 1916
The History

He named it Garran Hill.
The life he imagined happened elsewhere.

In February 1913, he bought a thousand-acre farm on land his father had logged a generation earlier. He gave it a name before the first stone was laid: Garran Hill.

"Build the farm, therefore; and let me hear at every stage of that happy game."

Weeks later, Wilson offered him London. The ambassadorship to the Court of St. James's. Page accepted -- and left. He directed the making of the house by letter, from three thousand miles away, while his son Ralph carried the work on the ground.

Leonard Tufts provided the craftsmen -- the same men building Pinehurst.

"Well, Frank, I did get here after all, didn't I?"
Aberdeen station · December 11, 1918

The Drawing Room

They made it bigger
so they could dance.

The fireplace wall runs nearly ten feet -- arched overmantel, built-in shelving, coffered ceiling above. Blue and white Delft tile. Georgian carved mantel.

Fire going.
No one home yet.
Hollycrest · 1959–1984

Betty Dumaine.
Twenty-five years.

In 1959, Elizabeth Dumaine purchased Hollycrest. Her Radcliffe roommate was Srinagarindra -- who became the Princess Mother of Thailand.

She lived here for twenty-five years. She kept a horse named Blue Fox.

Someone still puts flowers there.
